transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-28 14:00 UTC
Duration: 1:15
Attendees: Priya (AE), Sam (SE), Leah (Solutions), Marcus (Enablement) - Redwood; Jordan, Aisha, Tom, Maya, Luis - Northpoint
Recording note: internal enablement session; goal to refine messaging and practice a 6-minute demo arc focusing on dedicated vs hosted pitch and security objections.

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Goal: align on sellthrough narrative and practice micro-demo that emphasizes predictable latency, cost controls, and VPC/private options.
- Major objections rehearsed: "latency vs cost", "on-prem/VPC must-have", "audit logs/SOC2".
- Next: short demo clip, one-pager messaging, competitor rebut bullets, pilot stakeholder confirmation.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya (AE): Ok folks, thanks for carving time. We'll run about an hour plus, try to leave 10 at the end for notes. Today is more practice than a lecture, so, uh, feel free to interject.
[00:18] Jordan (Northpoint): Good, yeah thanks. We reeeally want the one-liner that sales can say in under fifteen seconds. It needs to land with execs and infra.
[00:27] Priya: Totally. Proposed one-liner — "Redwood Inference gives predictable, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so you can ship features without rebuilding serving infra." Is that too long?
[00:42] Aisha (Northpoint): It's good, but "predictable" is the word that sells to infra. Maybe put "predictable latency and unit economics" earlier.
[00:50] Sam (SE): Quick add — when we say "predictable" also hint at rollouts and fallbacks. Like "predictable performance with built-in fallbacks to keep apps live".
[01:04] Tom (Northpoint): Customers ask about quantization — they want to know if it's going to wreck quality.
[01:08] Leah (Redwood): Great spot, we should have an "impact tradeoff" line: "we provide quantization profiles tuned per model and workload to keep intent fidelity while cutting per-token cost up to X%" — avoids promising exact numbers.
[01:22] Marcus (Enablement): Also remember to speak to the model catalog. People confuse catalog with model control plane. Say: "curated open models + Redwood-verified perf profiles."
[01:34] Jordan: Mm, ok. Now demo practice — we have a 6-minute micro-demo. Sam, you want to run the happy path and then we'll throw security interrupts?
[01:42] Sam: Sure. I'll start with the hosted API path, then show dedicated pool config and a VPC/private control plane switchover. I'll try to show latency numbers in the console tabs real quick.
[01:55] [02:00] Sam (SE): All right sharing screen... um — note, the demo has a lot of tabs so I'll click through slowly. First, console, model list, show model "redwood-vast-7b" (note: transcript autoprobably says "redwood-vast-7b" which is a placeholder).
[02:18] Aisha: Call out the autoscale policy when you flip to dedicated. People like the commit/burst story.
[02:24] Sam: Good call. So I flip to Dedicated > pool config > autoscale policy: heavy read, steady push, burst allowed up to x nodes. Then show latency gauge: 95th percentile drops from 420ms to 110ms after dedicated.
[02:38] Luis: That 420 vs 110 number — we should avoid hard claims unless we add an asterisk. Sales will use those numbers verbatim.
[02:46] Priya: Right, Leah can craft a phrasing: "typical reductions observed in production classes; actual delta depends on model and sequence lengths."
[02:55] [03:00] Tom: Security interjection — show SSO and KMS. Customers want to see SAML, RBAC, and audit logs.
[03:07] Sam: Ok jumping to private control plane. Here we show SAML SSO configured, KMS integration, and audit logs stream. The audit logs view is a bit noisy but you can filter by token and route.
[03:22] Maya (Product): The audit log UX could be a pain point if we don't show the filter. Make sure to show the filter by token and the per-request latency columns.
[03:32] [03:45] Jordan: Let's roleplay an objection — "we can't send data off-prem due to compliance." Priya, how do you position Private?
[03:52] Priya: I say: "We offer a Private deployment with your VPC or an on-prem bundle; control plane can be customer-managed, keys in your KMS, and we support SOC2 Type II and audit exports. For air-gapped needs, our on-prem option packages the runtime and orchestration for your infra."
[04:08] Aisha: Good. Also add: "We can scope a short pilot with limited dataset residency to prove data flow and telemetry prior to full roll-out."
[04:16] Sam: Small technical note — sometimes transcription says "KV cache" as "KV cash" in notes; but in the demo we show prefix caching and continuous batching which helps latency.
[04:28] Leah: This is a good time to practice the competitive frame. Jordan, throw a competitor at us.
[04:33] Jordan: Ok, "How are you different from OpenAI?"
[04:36] Priya: Short answer: "OpenAI is model-first; Redwood is serve-first — we give you serving control, cost levers and rollouts so you can run reliably at scale without building infra."
[04:49] Sam: And add the observability piece: per-token cost visibility, trace by route, and automatic fallback policies.
[04:56] Tom: Anthropic pushes safety and model behavior — how do we position around that?
[05:00] Leah: Acknowledge: they are model-safety centric. Rebut: "If safety-first is the core ask, pair their models with Redwood's serving: our policy and eval tooling monitors quality regressions, and we support model-level controls for routing to safer variants."
[05:14] [05:30] Marcus: We're hearing a lot about "unit economics" — suggest a short template: "expected per-100k-token cost ranges for hosted vs dedicated vs private". Priya, can you own the numbers w/ a conservative band?
[05:41] Priya: I'll own a templated band but with the caveat: model + sequence length + caching changes it. I'll give a conservative estimate and call out variables.
[05:50] [06:00] Sam (demo restart): Ok re-running the micro-demo but this time I'm forcing a fallback path — primary GPU pool is 'full' and the router falls back to a quantized variant. Watch the latency and quality change.
[06:14] [06:30] Sam: Here you see a small drop in output confidence when we route to the quantized variant. We have eval hooks — auto-eval compares prompt set metrics and alerts if drift exceeds threshold.
[06:38] Aisha: Is that part of Redwood Optimize?
[06:40] Leah: Yes, it's under the Optimize toolkit — suggests quantization profiles and surfaces regressions for prompt sets.
[06:47] Jordan: The ask from our AEs is: how to answer "what if quantization breaks my NLU?"
[06:53] Priya: Reframe: show examples where quantization doesn't affect intent, and show evaluation metrics. Then offer a pilot with a small eval suite to prove parity.
[07:05] [07:15] Tom: Quick callout — show the rollback button during the demo. Executives like tangible control: deploy model X, run canary for N minutes, then rollback.
[07:24] Sam: Showing rollout UI now, click canary deploy, set traffic 10%, add monitoring hook, automatic fallback to previous variant on higher error rate.
[07:36] [07:50] Luis: Sales might want an "elevator objection path" — two lines to neutralize price and two lines for security. Let's craft those.
[07:58] Leah: For price: 1) "unit economics are controllable — choose dedicated pools and caching profiles to lower per-token cost", 2) "we help set the right quantization and batching defaults for your workload". For security: 1) "private control plane/VPC and KMS", 2) "audit logs and SSO with RBAC".
[08:20] Jordan: Let's run a rapid-fire roleplay. Aisha, you're the buyer with compliance stops. Priya you lead. Sam act technical.
[08:28] Aisha (roleplay): "We cannot risk external access to PHI. How can you guarantee data residency?"
[08:34] Priya (roleplay): "We'd scope a Private deployment in your VPC, keys remain in your KMS, and we can enable audit export for third-party review. We'll run a short pilot with the defined PII flows and add contractual DSRs."
[08:47] Aisha: Nice, but say "contractual DSRs" more plainly — "we'll put data residency, deletion, and access terms into the agreement."
[08:55] [09:00] Sam: Technical challenge — if they insist on air-gapped, our on-prem bundle requires more ops but it's doable; show the node diagram. (Sam gestures).
[09:10] Priya: Good. Now time check: we want to refine language for the one-pager and record a 6-min demo video. Marcus will own the recording plan.
[09:20] Marcus: I'll propose the storyboard: 0:00–0:45 one-liner + value props; 0:45–2:00 hosted happy path; 2:00–3:30 dedicated and autoscale; 3:30–4:30 private/VPC + security; 4:30–5:30 fallback/quantization; 5:30–6:00 recap + CTA.
[09:36] Leah: For the video, keep UI text large — the audit log table is hard to read at default zoom.
[09:44] [10:00] Jordan: Ok I'm going to note one linguistic tweak — avoid "we" heavy phrasing. Use customer-focused framing: "You get" vs "We provide."
[10:08] Priya: Nice. Also, let's prepare two closing slides for AEs: "If they care about cost" vs "If they care about security" — each with two bullets and a next-step CTA.
[10:19] [10:35] Tom: Can we add a quick benchmarking slide that outlines expected 95th-pct latency ranges for small, medium, large seq-lens? Not exact numbers but bands.
[10:44] Sam: Yes, but annotate with variables: model family, sequence length, batch size, caching hit rate.
[10:50] Marcus: Action item capture: I want a single shared deck we can PR against; we track changes and keep a short changelog.
[11:00] Leah: We'll also add two competitor rebut slides: one for OpenAI (model-first vs serve-first) and one for Anthropic (safety-first but pair with our serving).
[11:12] [11:30] Rapid-fire objections session continues — snippets captured: "What about pricing lock-ins?" "How long to onboard?" "SLA for dedicated?" Priya answers: typical onboarding 4–8 weeks for Dedicated, SLA options available on Dedicated, Hosted for fast POC.
[11:52] Maya (Product): Note for the demo: include a small trace showing per-token cost breakdown. Sales love dollar numbers even if approximated.
[12:02] Priya: We'll create a templated per-route token estimate for AEs to use — with a conservative band.
[12:12] [12:30] Sam: Technical deep-dive note — if a prospect asks about kernel selection/compilation optimizations, steer to research or SE deep dive. Keep the sell meeting concise.
[12:40] Jordan: Good. We're nearing the end. Let's summarize commitments.
[12:47] Priya (wrap): Commitments — Priya will share one-pager and pricing bands; Sam will record micro-demo clip; Leah will draft competitor bullets; Marcus will own the storyboard and recording plan; Jordan will confirm pilot stakeholder list and timeline.
[13:08] Aisha: Also ask legal for a short security pack — SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration notes — can we send a redacted pack?
[13:15] Leah: Yes we'll send the security pack link after we scrub customer-identifying bits.
[13:22] [13:30] Jordan: Ok great session. People found the roleplay helpful.
[13:36] Priya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
